name: Objectivism
summary: Objectivism is Ayn Rand's philosophy of reason, rational self-interest and individual rights. It holds that each person is an end in himself, that no one may initiate force against another, and that the only proper government is a minimal one protecting rights, under a regime of unregulated laissez-faire capitalism. It rejects faith, altruism, collectivism and anarchism.
scope: The philosophy as set out by Ayn Rand (The Virtue of Selfishness, Capitalism: The Unknown Ideal, Atlas Shrugged) and systematized by Leonard Peikoff, as presented by the Ayn Rand Institute and Atlas Society. It excludes libertarianism and anarcho-capitalism, which Rand rejected. Many social and foreign-policy answers are inferred from principles and carry low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Rights are negative claims to non-interference, so state-guaranteed medical care would force some to serve others and is rejected.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Objectivists oppose minimum-wage laws as interference in voluntary exchange.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Rand held that the value of work and goods is set by voluntary trade, and that government controls cause the harms blamed on markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Only laissez-faire capitalism with private ownership respects rights; the state should be separated from the economy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Objectivists oppose involuntary taxation and enforced redistribution, so higher taxes on any group to fund more state activity are opposed.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of coercion: voluntary unions are acceptable but Objectivists oppose compulsory-bargaining privileges and see collective claims skeptically.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Rand defended full, unregulated laissez-faire capitalism and held that regulation corrupts both state and market.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is derived from the right to life and is central to Objectivist politics.

cut-welfare.rationale: State welfare is enforced redistribution that Rand rejected, leaving the needy to voluntary charity; the dependency framing is secondary.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership arrangements should be left to voluntary contract, but a collective-ownership ideal is rejected as collectivism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: government exists to protect rights against aggressors, but Objectivists oppose treating innocent citizens as suspects.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the principle that force may be used only against those who initiate it, which implies consenting adult conduct is not the state's business.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Objectivists oppose all censorship, including legal limits on opinion.

strong-leader.rationale: Government must act under objective law with delegated powers; dictatorship is classed as statism.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: the right of self-defense follows from the right to life, so strict limits on peaceful ownership are disfavored.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and army are proper government functions and Objectivists favor a firm defense, but authority is confined to rights protection.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the non-initiation principle: voluntary adult exchange is not a matter for the law.

state-harmful.rationale: Rand rejected anarchism and held government is a necessary agent for protecting rights.

decide-locally.rationale: Objectivism cares about objective, rights-protecting law rather than the level of government at which it is made.

rehabilitation.rationale: Objectivists treat justice as retributive, including punishment of those who initiate force.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred: Rand rejected duty to groups and tradition as authority; family is a private matter, not a societal foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from individual rights and equal treatment under law; Objectivists do not oppose it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Rand championed legal abortion as a woman's right over her own body.

more-religion-public.rationale: Objectivists reject faith as a source of knowledge and oppose religious symbols and initiatives in government.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Objectivists oppose racism but regard affirmative action as legal racism and reject group claims.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed directly; Rand rejected feminism's collectivism but also biological determinism of mind.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred: Rand valued individual choice over inherited collective tradition, and Objectivists say immigration does not destroy culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Inferred: Rand rejected conservatism as defending an unprincipled status quo and called for principled change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Objectivist writers hold that immigration restrictions violate individual rights and favor open borders.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: world bodies would pool power beyond rights-protecting governments and are associated with altruism and statism.

free-trade.rationale: Rand named abolition of tariffs and trade barriers as the essence of capitalism's foreign policy.

nation-first.rationale: Rand wanted a self-interested but trading foreign policy, so adherents would not endorse either side of this framing.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Altruism is said to justify intervention abroad, which Objectivists reject; force is justified for national self-defense.

open-borders.rationale: ARI-aligned writers favor open immigration in a free society, though borders matter for a rights-protecting state.

limit-growth.rationale: Objectivists see production and industrial progress as virtuous and reject environmentalist limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Objectivists oppose most government environmental regulation as forced moral views.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from Rand's celebration of reason and industrial production.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from support for industrial energy production and opposition to environmental restrictions.

revolution-justified.rationale: Inferred: a people may resist a government that violates rights, though Rand urged opposing unjust law through ideas.

experts-over-public.rationale: Objectivists reject rule by officials and by majorities alike; objective law, not experts, constrains power.

central-planning.rationale: Central planning violates individual rights and is statism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Private ownership is part of capitalism's justification; public or collective ownership is rejected even with markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: Involuntary taxation is opposed, and the land tax is no exception.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Property rights extend to disposal of property, and Objectivists oppose compulsory taxation beyond a minimal state.

basic-income.rationale: Rand rejected the unearned and enforced redistribution.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state should be separated from the economy; Rand attacked the aristocracy of pull and government favors.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rand defended big business and held that how property is distributed should result from voluntary trade, not policy.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wage labor and trade are core to capitalism as Rand defended it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from separating state and economics, which includes money; Rand's advocates favor gold-based money, not opened here.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies setting wages and prices are statism.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rule by a party guided by an ideology violates rights; dictatorship is statism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred: government legitimacy comes from the consent of the governed, not heredity.

democracy-best.rationale: Unlimited democracy is classed as statism; the limits on government are rights, not majorities.

direct-votes.rationale: Majority rule over rights is rejected; government is bound to objective law.

workers-councils.rationale: Rights-protecting government under objective law, not class-based bodies, is the basis for power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Individual rights, not regional claims, matter; a free region might secede but an unfree one would not be endorsed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rand rejected rule by an elite; legitimate government acts as the citizens' agent.

political-violence-never.rationale: Force is justified in retaliation against those who initiate it, so political violence is not never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Rand cast the warrior as the antagonist of the trader and said capitalism alone bans force.

separate-church-state.rationale: Objectivists want strict separation and oppose faith-based initiatives and religious symbols in government.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Faith and mysticism are rejected as sources of knowledge; law should follow objective rights.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rand rejected anarchism; private marketed courts and police would be a miscarriage of justice.

military-superiority.rationale: A firm, assertive defense of free nations is part of the ARI reading of Rand.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rand held that interests of rational individuals do not conflict and rejected Marxism; ideas, not class, drive history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rights are to freedom of action, not results.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Collective and group rights are rejected, and property rests on individual rights.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred: collective guilt and group claims are rejected.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred: group identity is not a legitimate basis for politics.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Rand proudly advocated rational selfishness as the moral standard.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rand held that no one owes the community a sacrifice and that the individual is an end in himself.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Objectivism holds value exists only relative to living beings and nature has no value apart from human purposes.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred: coercive population control violates rights and Objectivists see human life as the standard of value.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Rand defended industrial civilization and called environmentalism an anti-industrial revolution.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from admiration for production and reason; institutions are not valued in themselves.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from freedom of action over one's own life and body.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: government is a limited agent under objective law, not a decision-maker over life.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the primacy of private property and individual rights against the state.

restore-past-order.rationale: Rand attacked conservatism and sought principled change rather than return.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred: Rand insisted on principles over expediency, but her stance on pragmatism was not opened here.

direct-action.rationale: Unjust laws are opposed through ideas, not martyrdom or force.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred from the principle that force cannot achieve a free society and persuasion by reason must.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Objectivism holds reason and production are the means of human survival and flourishing.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Trade among independent producers is central to the trader principle.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Rand rejected the demand for the unearned.

production-for-use.rationale: Profit is the legitimate reward for productive work.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Value of work is set by voluntary trade, so profit is earned, not exploited.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dictatorship is statism and class rule violates individual rights.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rand argued laissez-faire capitalism is the only system that bans force, and so causes peace.

taxation-theft.rationale: Objectivists oppose involuntary taxation and favor voluntary funding of government, though Rand did not call it theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Close to the non-initiation principle: force only against those who initiate force.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rejects collective rights; rights belong to individuals.

conscription.rationale: Rand called the draft an abrogation of rights.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Objectivism relies on rights and objective law, not on exit, as the check on government.

state-as-business.rationale: Government is a monopoly on retaliatory force with limited functions, not a business with customers.

media-academia-power.rationale: Rand stressed the power of intellectuals over culture, but not that they outrank elected officials; not opened here.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racism is condemned as collectivism; individuals are judged on their own character.

organic-representation.rationale: Rights-based representation of individuals, not group bodies, is the standard.

total-state.rationale: Total state control is the opposite of Rand's position.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rand sought an intellectual renaissance rather than a national one.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The warrior is the antagonist of the trader; only defensive force is legitimate.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule must follow objective law, not personal oaths.

knowledge-power.rationale: Rand held that objective knowledge is possible through reason and that objectivity is neither intrinsic nor subjective.

universal-morality.rationale: Ethics is objective and applies to all humans because it is rooted in human nature.

single-common-good.rationale: Rand rejected the collective good as a standard; rational interests are individual, not one common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed directly; self-determination only for free nations, with no ethnic claim.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred: an ethnic-group claim to citizenship is a collective claim, though individuals may immigrate freely.

revive-national-language.rationale: Inferred: the state should not direct culture or language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Owners decide how firms are run; majority votes over property violate rights.

school-vouchers.rationale: Objectivists oppose public education, and publicly funded vouchers remain tax-funded.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from opposition to government economic management.

economic-freedom.rationale: Rand held that political freedom requires economic freedom and the separation of state and economics.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule must come from objective, enforceable law, not the moral example of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Free nations alone have a right to self-determination, so the claim is conditional.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred: a free nation need not seek approval from a world body to defend its rights.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Rand held reason is the only absolute and the only source of knowledge, rejecting faith and mysticism.

missingStatements.text: Reason, not faith or emotion, should be the only guide to knowledge and action.
missingStatements.rationale: Rand held reason is the only absolute and the only source of knowledge, rejecting faith and mysticism.

notes: Rand rejected libertarianism; the ARI and Atlas Society differ on some points such as open immigration and foreign policy.
